items.abstract: <jats:p>Industrial image anomaly detection plays a crucial role in quality control for intelligent manufacturing. Although unsupervised methods based on reverse distillation have achieved promising performance on standard benchmark datasets, they remain vulnerable to domain shifts in real industrial scenarios. Factors such as illumination variation, noise interference, and blur degradation can disrupt the distribution of normal features, leading to increased false positives, while subtle or small-scale anomalies are easily obscured, resulting in missed detections. To address these issues, this paper proposes an expert-guided reverse distillation method for cross-domain industrial image anomaly detection. Built upon the reverse distillation framework, the proposed method jointly improves teacher encoder robustness and student decoder detail reconstruction. Specifically, an expert guider with the same architecture as the teacher encoder and frozen parameters is introduced to constrain the teacher, thereby enhancing the consistency and compactness of teacher features under normalsamples and common distribution shifts and providing a stable normal reference for teacher-student residual computation. Meanwhile, on the student side, a one-class bottleneck embedding module, distribution-specific compensation, and distributioninvariant filtering are incorporated to maintain stable detection performance under cross-domain conditions. Furthermore, to alleviate the insufficient fine-grained information recovery caused by the absence of skip connections in conventional reverse distillation, an offset-aware guided expert information injection mechanism is designed. According to the degree of domain shift, shallow expert features are adaptively injected into the student decoder, which enhances residual responses to subtle anomalies while suppressing the introduction of domain-specific disturbances. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior imagelevel detection and pixel-level localization performance over existing methods in multiple out-of-distribution scenarios on the MVTec-AD dataset, while effectivelyreducing missed detections of weak anomalies and small-scale defects without sacrificing cross-domain robustness.</jats:p>
title: Expert-Guided Reverse Distillation for Cross-Domain Industrial Image Anomaly Detection

items.abstract: <jats:p>The complex nature of industrial processes causes fluctuations in data distribution, which are called domain shifts. Training a single machine learning model on data with domain shifts leads to performance degradation. On the other hand, gathering enough data to build separate models for each domain could be impossible. Anomaly detection plays a crucial role in health management and failure detection, enabling reliable and safe operation of industrial systems. In this work, we propose a method for anomaly detection that integrates domain shift detection with unsupervised domain adaptation called DASAD (Drift Aware Streaming Anomaly Detection). The approach automatically identifies breakpoints in multivariate data stream distributions to dynamically define source and target domains, eliminating the need for predefined domain boundaries. The knowledge is then transferred from the source domain to the target domain to compensate for changes in manufacturing line operation and maintain satisfactory performance despite limited data in the target domains. The feasibility of our approach was presented in a real–world steel industry case. The evaluation was carried out on data from a cold rolling mill simulator.</jats:p>
title: Addressing Representation and Aggregation Biases in Streaming Anomaly Detection through Domain Adaptation and Domain Shift Detection

items.abstract: The goal of \ac{UAD} is to detect anomalous signals under the condition that only non-anomalous ({\it normal}) data is available beforehand. In UAD under Domain-Shift Conditions (UAD-S), data is further exposed to contextual changes that are usually unknown beforehand. Motivated by the difficulties encountered in the \acs{UAD-S} task presented at the 2021 edition of the \ac{DCASE} challenge\footnote{DCASE website: \url{http://dcase.community}}, we visually inspect \acp{UMAP} for log-STFT, log-mel and pretrained \ac{L3} representations of the \ac{DCASE} \acs{UAD-S} dataset. In our exploratory investigation, we look for two qualities, {\it \ac{SEP}} and {\it \ac{DSUP}}, and formulate several hypotheses that could facilitate diagnosis and developement of further representation and detection approaches. Particularly, we hypothesize that input length and pretraining may regulate a relevant tradeoff between \ac{SEP} and \ac{DSUP}. Our code as well as the resulting \acp{UMAP} and plots are publicly available\footnote{Online Resources:\\ Code: \url{https://github.com/andres-fr/dcase2021_umaps}\\Webpage: \url{https://ai4s.surrey.ac.uk/2021/dcase_uads}}.
title: USING UMAP TO INSPECT AUDIO DATA FOR UNSUPERVISED ANOMALY DETECTION UNDER DOMAIN-SHIFT CONDITIONS

items.abstract: <jats:p>Industrial visual anomaly detection is a key capability for automated quality inspection, yet practical systems must simultaneously localize subtle defects and provide human-interpretable explanations. Recent vision-language pipelines couple a frozen multimodal encoder with a Large Language Model (LLM) to enable joint pixel-level scoring and text responses, but their cross-modal alignment and prompt construction remain lightweight and can lead to ambiguous anomaly maps or unstable "normal/abnormal" decisions. This paper proposes AlignPromptGPT, a lightweight prompt-enhanced framework that preserves the overall AnomalyGPT architecture while improving two critical components. First, an EnhancedLinearLayer augments the original linear projector with a residual non-linear branch, strengthening patch-to-text alignment for fine-grained defects. Second, a PromptMaker compresses intermediate visual features into position-sensitive prompt tokens and introduces an anomaly-aware scaling mechanism, guiding the LLM to focus on defective regions and generate more consistent explanations. Experiments on MVTec AD show that AlignPromptGPT achieves 96.25% I-AUROC and 89.16% P-AUROC, and improves the accuracy of image-level textual judgements to 86.27%. Moreover, the fine-tuned checkpoint is reduced to 20.3 MB, and the inference throughput is improved to 1.57 FPS on a single RTX 4090D. These results demonstrate that AlignPromptGPT delivers accurate, efficient, and interpretable industrial anomaly detection.</jats:p>
title: AlignPromptGPT: Aligned Prompting for Industrial Image Anomaly Detection

                    Industrial anomaly detection systems deployed in production environments face domain shift from lighting changes, sensor degradation, and material variations, which silently degrade detection accuracy. items.abstract: <jats:p>Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) in Industrial Control Systems (ICS) exploit vulnerabilities across operational layers, leveraging stealthiness mechanisms that make them fundamentally difficult to detect using single-domain approaches. While multi-domain anomaly detection has shown promise, existing studies focus on single-stage attacks, leaving realistic APT scenarios largely unexplored, partly due to the inability of companies to release representative operational data. This work addresses that gap by deploying an Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS), an industrial control system that measures electrical parameters across facility infrastructure integrating multiple industrial protocols, in collaboration with an industrial partner, and subjecting it to realistic APT campaigns to provide the multi-domain labelled data needed to study ICS-specific APT detection under operationally representative conditions. This paper presents three contributions: (i) a structured analysis of ICS-specific APTs establishing taxonomies of detection mechanisms, stealthiness mechanisms, and operational impact from documented real-world campaigns, directly informing the design of the dataset that follows; (ii) EPMS-APT&apos;26, the first labelled dataset of realistic ICS-specific APT campaigns collected from a physical three-layer testbed built in collaboration with an industrial partner, capturing multi-stage kill chains across both network and physical domains; (iii) a systematic benchmarking of single-domain and multi-domain anomaly detection approaches across SWaT&apos;16, SWaT&apos;19, and EPMS-APT&apos;26. Our evidence-grounded conclusions on the conditions under which existing approaches succeed or fail provide practitioners and researchers with a principled basis for selecting detection strategies. Results indicate that existing approaches exhibit significant limitations when faced with realistic ICS-specific APT campaigns, pointing to fundamental gaps in current detection methodologies.</jats:p>
title: Multi-Domain Anomaly Detection for Advanced Persistent Threat Detection in Industrial Control Systems

items.abstract: <jats:p>Federated learning enables distributed clients to collaboratively train a shared model without exposing raw data, making it a promising paradigm for intelligent Internet of Things (IoT) and edge-network systems. However, its open and distributed training process is vulnerable to poisoning attacks, where malicious or compromised clients inject poisoned samples or upload manipulated model updates to distort global aggregation and degrade model performance. Existing defenses mainly rely on robust aggregation, similarity measurement, or statistical anomaly detection. Although effective in near-IID settings, these methods often deteriorate in practical heterogeneous environments, where clients usually hold non-IID data due to diverse sensing conditions, device types, user behaviors, and deployment locations. Such natural update divergence reduces the separability between benign and malicious updates, making poisoning detection more challenging. To address this issue, this paper proposes FedSDC, a robust federated learning defense framework based on reliability-aware client selection, domain-shift elimination, and clustered anomaly detection. FedSDC first reduces the participation probability of historically suspicious clients. It then aligns client representations in a shared feature space to mitigate domain-induced update divergence and make benign updates more compact. Finally, it performs cluster-level anomalous gradient detection by grouping clients with similar update directions and suppressing updates that deviate from the mainstream direction within each cluster. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedSDC achieves stronger robustness and higher test accuracy than representative robust aggregation baselines, verifying its effectiveness for poisoning defense in heterogeneous federated learning.</jats:p>
title: Robust Federated Learning for Intelligent IoT Networks via Domain-Shift Elimination and Clustered Anomaly Detection

items.abstract: <jats:p>We present Seeing Voices, a cross-modal framework for unsupervised industrial audio anomaly detection that requires no audio-specific training. Our key insight is that mature vision-domain anomaly detectors, pre-trained on ImageNet, can be directly applied to audio if the signal is cast into an appropriate visual representation. We introduce SoundFrames: a three-channel RGB image encoding the log-mel spectrogram (R), its temporal derivative ∆-mel (G), and instantaneous phase (B), designed so that mechanical faults disrupt all three channels in visually detectable ways. Applying PatchCore-a state-of-the-art image anomaly detector-to SoundFrames with zero audio fine-tuning, we achieve AUC = 1.000 on both fan and bearing machine types from the DCASE 2022 Task 2 benchmark. Beyond detection accuracy, we introduce GradCAM back-projection: because the SoundFrame's horizontal axis encodes time and vertical axis encodes frequency, the vision model's gradient saliency map projects directly onto the original audio timeline, yielding interpretable time-frequency anomaly localisation unavailable in prior audio anomaly detection work. We further provide a systematic round-trip fidelity analysis quantifying information preservation through the audio → image → audio pipeline.</jats:p>
title: Seeing Voices: Cross-Modal Audio-to-Image Translation for Zero-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection

items.abstract: <jats:p>Industrial image anomaly detection plays a critical role in intelligent manufacturing by automatically identifying defective products through visual inspection. While unsupervised approaches eliminate dependency on annotated anomaly samples, current teacher–student framework-based methods still face two fundamental limitations: insufficient discriminative capability for structural anomalies and suboptimal anomaly feature decoupling efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose a Synthetic-Anomaly Contrastive Distillation (SACD) framework for industrial anomaly detection. SACD comprises two pivotal components: (1) a reverse distillation (RD) paradigm whereby a pre-trained teacher network extracts hierarchically structured representations, subsequently guiding the student network with inverse architectural configuration to establish hierarchical feature alignment; (2) a group of feature calibration (FeaCali) modules designed to refine the student’s outputs by eliminating anomalous feature responses. During training, SACD adopts a dual-branch strategy, where one branch encodes multi-scale features from defect-free images, while a Siamese anomaly branch processes synthetically corrupted counterparts. FeaCali modules are trained to strip out a student’s anomalous patterns in anomaly branches, enhancing the student network’s exclusive modeling of normal patterns. We construct a dual-objective optimization integrating cross-model distillation loss and intra-model contrastive loss to train SACD for feature alignment and discrepancy amplification. At the inference stage, pixel-wise anomaly scores are computed through multi-layer feature discrepancies between the teacher’s representations and the student’s refined outputs. Comprehensive evaluations on the MVTec AD and BTAD benchmark demonstrate that our method is effective and superior to current knowledge distillation-based approaches.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study presents an enhanced unified feature representation for classical one-class anomaly detection in industrial image inspection using the MVTec AD dataset. Experiments were conducted on all fifteen categories of the MVTec AD dataset, including object and texture categories. Unlike raw pixel-based representations, the proposed feature representation integrates raw intensity information, histogram of oriented gradients (HOG), local binary pattern (LBP), gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM)-based texture descriptors, and basic statistical intensity features. These complementary descriptors were evaluated with classical one-class anomaly detection methods, including PCA-based reconstruction, kNN-density, Local Outlier Factor, One-Class SVM with RBF kernel, Isolation Forest, and Mahalanobis-PCA. Considering the class imbalance inherent in anomaly detection tasks, Average Precision (AP) was used as the primary evaluation metric, while ROC-AUC and F1@95%-training-quantile were reported as supporting metrics. The results showed that PCA-based reconstruction achieved the strongest overall performance with a mean ROC-AUC of 0.8289, mean AP of 0.9254, and mean F1@95%-training-quantile of 0.8343. Category-based analyses showed particularly strong discrimination in the bottle, toothbrush, leather, transistor, and zipper categories, whereas carpet, screw, and grid remained more challenging. The findings indicate that carefully designed classical feature representations can provide an explainable and CPU-friendly baseline for industrial anomaly detection, particularly at the model-inference stage, while feature extraction remains the dominant computational cost.</jats:p>
